_doc: HMTc Category 26 (Peptides, SARMs, and Research Chemicals) compiler config — Method v2.0, no-regulatory-anchor (control) form. This class is legally distinct: the products are unapproved/misbranded drugs sold outside the dietary-supplement and food frameworks, so NO jurisdiction sets a lawful product heavy-metal CONTENT limit for them. Under Method v2.0 the standard is normally min(pooled percentile, strictest government ceiling); here the ceiling term does not exist, and per the Part 2/Part 19 firewall the pooled-percentile (occurrence) term is a STAFF-side workbench quantity that must never be published as a product-content limit. The Step Zero lock (docs/governance/category-26-step0-lock.md) resolves this: every panel cell is `control` (mandatory per-lot testing + a published analytical method + a toxicology-anchored escalation rule, with NO occurrence-derived or product-content number), except methylmercury, which is a substantiated `not_material` determination. The route-appropriate ICH Q3D / USP <232> permitted daily exposures (PDEs, ug/day) are attached to each control cell as a TOXICOLOGICAL anchor for the escalation rule only — injectable rows carry the parenteral PDE, oral rows the oral PDE, and nasal/sublingual (mucosal) rows the most-protective of the parenteral and inhalation PDE per analyte. A PDE is a daily-dose toxicology reference, not a ug/kg product-content limit, and is never converted into one. HMTc certifies heavy-metal SAFETY only for this class; it does not endorse, approve, or vouch for the efficacy or legality of the products (Karen's public-protection decision, 2026-08-13). See CLAUDE.md Part 2 (firewall), Part 19 (Method v2.0), and project memory project_cat26_peptides_certify_public_protection.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 — no-regulatory-anchor (control) form. Government-limit lookup returns nothing for this class, so cells resolve to `control` or a substantiated `not_material`; ICH Q3D / USP <232> route-appropriate PDEs are toxicological anchors only, never product-content limits.
reference_method: ICP-MS per USP General Chapter <233> (or an equivalently validated ICP-MS / ICP-OES elemental method) on the finished product in its as-sold form: total-element quantitation for the eight totals (Pb, Cd, tAs, tHg, Ni, Sn, Al, total Cr), with reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) on an elevated total-arsenic result and reflex hexavalent-chromium speciation on an elevated total-chromium result.
tier_note: Tiers follow the toxicology-based HMTc framework (project_hmtc_status_tier_framework): Tier 1 = Pb, Cd, iAs, MeHg (no safe threshold; zero tolerance for exceeding the escalation anchor). Total As and total Hg are Tier-1-adjacent screens for their toxic species (iAs; inorganic Hg is an ICH Q3D Class-1 toxicant). Tier 2 = Ni, Sn, Al, Cr-VI (established tolerable intakes / acute-not-chronic; the Status B 150% transitional band applies). Total Cr is the screen for the Tier-2 hexavalent species.

vacuum_scan.note: The compiler scans data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv for any credible-jurisdiction product-CONTENT heavy-metal limit whose product_scope matches this class. Method v2.0 predicts none exist (this is the regulatory vacuum that gives an HMTc mark its highest consumer-protection value here). A hit would REBUT the no-anchor premise and is treated as a build-blocking defect so the vacuum claim is proven, not assumed. ICH Q3D / USP <232> pharmaceutical PDEs are daily-exposure toxicology references for APPROVED drug products, not product-content limits for this gray-market class, and are correctly absent from the product-content register.

control_template.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a lawful product heavy-metal content limit for this unapproved-drug class, so the Method v2.0 min(percentile, ceiling) rule loses its ceiling term and the occurrence (percentile) term is a firewalled staff quantity that must not be published as a product-content limit. HMTc therefore controls {analyte_label} by mandatory testing rather than a published concentration number: every certified lot is quantified by the reference method, and the result is judged against the route-appropriate toxicological anchor below, not against a fixed ug/kg cap. The absence of any regulatory backstop is precisely why an independent heavy-metal-safety mark carries its highest consumer-protection value for this class.
control_template.escalation: Escalation is toxicological, not a fixed concentration. Using the product's labeled or manufacturer-directed single dose and maximum daily dosing, the measured {analyte_label} concentration is converted to an implied elemental daily intake (ug/day) and compared to the {route_label} ICH Q3D / USP <232> permitted daily exposure. A result whose implied daily intake reaches or exceeds that PDE is an automatic certification failure. Tier-1 analytes carry zero tolerance for PDE exceedance (Status C or worse immediately); Tier-2 analytes are eligible for the Status B transitional band (up to 150% of the anchor, with a documented remediation plan) before failure. Any detection above the method reporting limit — even well below the anchor — triggers a documented source investigation and a repeat-lot verification, because a contaminant present at all in a synthetic product signals an uncontrolled raw material, catalyst, or reagent.

speciation_notes.tAs: Total arsenic is the ICP-MS screen. The ICH Q3D arsenic PDE is set on INORGANIC arsenic as the worst case, so an elevated total-As result triggers reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS); the iAs cell carries the health-relevant anchor.
speciation_notes.iAs: Inorganic arsenic is the toxic species and the form expected from synthesis reagents, catalysts, and solvents. Its anchor is the ICH Q3D arsenic PDE (which is defined on iAs). Reported as a reflex speciation on an elevated total-As screen.
speciation_notes.Cr: Total chromium is the ICP-MS screen. Its anchor is the route-appropriate ICH Q3D chromium PDE. An elevated total-Cr result triggers reflex hexavalent-chromium speciation; the Cr-VI cell carries the carcinogenic-species anchor.
speciation_notes.Cr-VI: Hexavalent chromium is the carcinogenic species. Its escalation anchor is the 3 ug/day ICH Q3D chromium INHALATION PDE, the value the guideline set low specifically for Cr(VI) carcinogenicity, applied as the most-protective anchor for the hexavalent species across every route. Reported as a reflex speciation on an elevated total-Cr screen.

parenteral.framework: FDA 21 CFR 201.323 (aluminium in large- and small-volume parenterals)
parenteral.basis: finished parenteral solution as administered (LVP ceiling 25 ug/L; SVP and pharmacy-bulk packages carry at-expiry aluminium labeling and validation)
parenteral.note: Aluminium is not an ICH Q3D / USP <232> element. The FDA parenteral-aluminium rule is the ONE sovereign product framework that reaches any product in this class, and it reaches only the injected route; it is cited as the route-appropriate regulatory/toxicological anchor for the escalation rule and is NOT converted into a ug/kg product-content limit for the dry powder or oil. Craven 2025 measured injectable-AAS aluminium at mean 47.31 ug/mL (up to 110 ug/mL), orders of magnitude above the 25 ug/L parenteral-solution reference once diluted to an injection volume.

oral.framework: JECFA provisional tolerable weekly intake 2 mg Al/kg body weight/week; EFSA tolerable weekly intake 1 mg Al/kg body weight/week
oral.basis: chronic dietary intake reference (mg/kg body weight/week)
oral.note: No government sets a per-product oral aluminium content limit outside the lone FSANZ infant-formula entry, so the oral anchor is the intake-based tolerable weekly intake. Craven 2025 measured oral-AAS aluminium at mean 651 ug/g (up to 1220 ug/g), the single highest toxic-metal load in the survey; at gram-scale oral dosing this can consume a large share of the tolerable weekly intake. The intake reference anchors the escalation rule and is not a product-content limit.

mucosal.framework: FDA 21 CFR 201.323 (parenteral aluminium) as the most-protective systemic anchor, with the JECFA/EFSA aluminium tolerable weekly intake as the intake reference
mucosal.basis: systemic absorption reference; nasal/sublingual absorption bypasses first-pass gut metabolism
mucosal.note: Aluminium is not an ICH Q3D element and no government sets a mucosal aluminium product limit. The parenteral framework is applied as the most-protective systemic anchor because mucosal absorption skips the gut's absorption discount, with the tolerable weekly intake as the chronic reference. Not a product-content limit.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation, source, or reaction pathway in the abiotic synthetic manufacture of peptides, SARMs, anabolic-androgenic steroids, or research chemicals. Methylmercury is produced by microbial biomethylation in aquatic and sediment environments and enters the human food supply through marine bioaccumulation; there is no biomethylation step in chemical synthesis, purification, or reconstitution. Any mercury contamination of these products is inorganic or elemental mercury introduced by reagents, catalysts, or apparatus, and is fully captured by the total-mercury (tHg) control cell. ICH Q3D itself sets the mercury PDE on inorganic mercury as the worst case for pharmaceutical elemental impurities, confirming that inorganic, not organic, mercury is the relevant species for a manufactured product. This is a no-pathway determination (absence of a formation route), corroborated by the total-Hg control that bounds any organomercury fraction.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury product limit for pharmaceuticals or research chemicals; ICH Q3D / USP <232> control mercury as inorganic Hg. Bounded by the tHg total-mercury control cell.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: ICH Q3D / USP <232> (inorganic-Hg basis); FDA (unapproved-drug status, no MeHg product limit); no food/supplement MeHg instrument applies to a synthetic non-marine product
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury quantitation by ICP-MS (the tHg control); no methylmercury speciation is defined for a synthetic product with no biomethylation pathway.

peptides-injectable-hormones.name: Injectable peptide hormones (GLP-1 analogs, GH secretagogues, synthetic peptides)
peptides-injectable-hormones.scope_note: Gray-market injectable peptide hormones sold outside the drug-approval and supplement frameworks: GLP-1 receptor-agonist analogs, growth-hormone secretagogues, and other synthetic peptides supplied as lyophilised powder for reconstitution or as ready-to-inject solution. The injected route bypasses gut absorption, so per microgram it is the most severe pathway in the taxonomy and the escalation anchor is the parenteral ICH Q3D PDE. Collagen and protein-hydrolysate peptides with a Supplement Facts panel route to Category 16, not here.

sarms-oral.name: Oral SARMs
sarms-oral.scope_note: Selective androgen receptor modulators supplied as oral capsules, tablets, or liquid droppers, sold as research chemicals outside any drug-approval or supplement framework. The oral route carries the larger per-gram toxic-metal burden in the seed evidence (Craven 2025: oral nickel mean 27.48 ug/g, near the 200 ug/day oral PDE depending on dose; oral aluminium mean 651 ug/g), so the escalation anchor is the oral ICH Q3D PDE.

aas-injectable.name: Injectable anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS)
aas-injectable.scope_note: Illicit injectable anabolic-androgenic steroids supplied as oil-based solutions (testosterone esters, nandrolone, trenbolone, and similar), sold outside any drug-approval framework. The direct evidence anchor is Craven 2025 (16 injectable oils: lead in every sample, cadmium quantifiable only in injectables, aluminium mean 47.31 ug/mL). The injected route bypasses gut absorption, so the escalation anchor is the parenteral ICH Q3D PDE.

research-chem-raw-powders.name: Raw AAS / peptide powders (pre-formulation)
research-chem-raw-powders.route_label: parenteral (most-protective; a pre-formulation raw material may be reconstituted for injection)
research-chem-raw-powders.scope_note: Bulk raw powders (active pharmaceutical ingredient grade or lower) sold pre-formulation for home reconstitution into injectable oils or oral preparations. Because the same powder may be reconstituted for injection, the most-protective route is applied and the escalation anchor is the parenteral ICH Q3D PDE, consistent with the Step Zero lock's treatment of the parenteral pathway as the most severe. Craven 2025 analysed 2 raw powders (lead 1.18 ug/g; aluminium 51.73 ug/g).

peptides-nasal-sublingual.name: Nasal/sublingual/troche gray-market peptide preparations (mucosal route)
peptides-nasal-sublingual.scope_note: Gray-market peptide preparations delivered across a mucosal membrane: nasal sprays, sublingual drops, and troches/lozenges. Mucosal absorption bypasses first-pass gut metabolism (like injection) and the nasal fraction adds a local respiratory pathway, so the escalation anchor is the most-protective of the parenteral and inhalation ICH Q3D PDE per analyte. No route-specific direct occurrence data yet; the contamination mechanism (overseas unregulated synthesis, no GMP) is shared with the injectable and oral rows.
